why:
Use the Advance repertoire as White against the French and Caro-Kann. Occupy the centre with both pawns, then advance the e-pawn when Black challenges with the d-pawn. The d4 pawn supports e5, giving you space but also creating a pawn chain that Black can undermine.

The two defences are not identical. In the French, Black has already put the e-pawn on e6, restricting the c8 bishop. In the Caro-Kann, Black can develop that bishop before moving the e-pawn. The guide keeps those structures separate. Your existing Caro-Kann repertoire is still your training as Black, not replaced by these White lines.

Space is not a forced attack. Defend the base of the chain, finish development and answer pawn breaks concretely. If exchanges change the centre, reassess the position rather than trying to preserve a memorized shape at any cost.
